Physics: Keys and numerical data check out across the section, but the coverage is badly skewed: roughly fifteen mechanics/kinematics items and six circuit items, four near-identical interference-intensity questions and two conduction-ratio questions, while magnetism, EMI, AC, ray optics, semiconductors and gravitation are untested. Every topic tag is mismatched to its actual question (e.g. Q1 "Rotational Motion" is vertical projection, Q10 "Alternating Current" is YDSE), so the whole tag set must be reassigned before printing. Difficulty is mostly easy one- or two-step recall-application, with nothing exceeding the 90-second budget, so a few items (e.g. Q3, Q8, Q30) could be raised to BITSAT level while the duplicates are replaced.
[major] This is the same one-step calculation as Q9 (I = 4I₀cos²(δ/2) for two equal coherent sources), so one of the pair must be replaced with a genuinely different wave-optics item.
[minor] The vector notation is corrupted LaTeX (backslashes lost, printing as "mathbf{F}", "mathbf{i}", "hat{mathbf{n}}"), which must be repaired before printing.
[minor] A "person of mass 2 kg" is physically absurd; call it a 2 kg point mass/small object (the numbers and key are otherwise correct).
[major] Essentially duplicates Q18 (steady-state heat current scaling as kA/L), so replace it with an item from an untested chapter.
[major] This is a third repetition of the Q9/Q15 interference-intensity formula (extra path → phase → cos² factor) and should be swapped for a different topic.
[minor] "In two frictionless trials, a block of mass m ... In the other trial" is unidiomatic and confusing; it should read "In one of two frictionless trials ... in the other ...".

Chemistry: Coverage is broad and well spread across physical, inorganic and organic chemistry, and most numerical items (Q48, 50, 59, 62, 67, 68, 77, 78) are correctly keyed and sit at the right 60–90 s difficulty. However, the section leans heavily on five near-identical "which statements are correct" items and several pure-recall questions, while two items (Q45 ordering ambiguity, Q60 lanthanide Landé moment) are unsound or out of level and Q47/Q75 and Q51/Q69 pair up as redundant concept tests. Fixing the two ambiguous items, the LaTeX corruption in Q51/Q76, and replacing one of each duplicate pair would make this a printable, well-balanced section.

[major] "Increasing numerical electron gain enthalpy" naturally reads as magnitude, under which options A and B are also wrong (Cl 349 > F 328 > Br 325 > I 295; S 200 > Se 195 > Te 190 > O 141), so the key is not unique unless the stem explicitly says algebraic/signed values.
[minor] The species is coded as `$\text{XeF}_4$` with the backslash lost ("$ ext{XeF}_4$"), so the formula will print as garbled text.
[minor] The stem hands over the entire Lucas-test rule, reducing the item to noticing that butan-2-ol is secondary; drop the rule sentence so it actually tests recall.

[major] The 9.72 BM key requires the Landé factor μ = g√(J(J+1)), which is beyond BITSAT level, while the spin-only formula taught at this level gives option A (6.93 BM), leaving two defensible answers.
[minor] This tests exactly the same VSEPR lone-pair geometry skill as Q51 (shape/hybridisation of XeF4); swap one of them for a different bonding concept such as MO bond order or dipole moment.

[major] The relative SN1 ranking of benzyl chloride and 2-chloro-2-methylpropane is genuinely contested (measured solvolysis rates favour the tertiary halide), so both A and B are defensible and the comparison must be removed.

[major] This duplicates Q47, which already tests high-spin/low-spin d6 Fe(II) with the same weak-field aqua and strong-field cyanide ligands; replace it with another coordination topic (isomerism, CFSE, or EAN).
[minor] Literal "\n" sequences and stray "$"/"$$" delimiters run the statements together in broken math mode, so the statement list must be re-typeset.

English Proficiency: The section covers the expected BITSAT English spread — agreement, tense, verb complementation, voice, vocabulary, idiom, rearrangement and a two-question comprehension set — with no wrong keys and an appropriately short reading passage. Difficulty is skewed low, however: q85, q87, q89 and q90 are near-giveaways with implausible distractors, while only q82 and q93 demand real lexical reasoning. Raise the ceiling on two or three of the easy items and resolve the double-answer rearrangement in q91 before printing.

[minor] The sentence is marked into four parts (I–IV) but only Parts I–III are offered as options, so the option set is inconsistent with the labelling — either merge Part IV into III or add it as an option.

[minor] The distractors ("careless route", "ordinary route", "silent route") do not collocate at all, so the item is answerable without any vocabulary knowledge; use plausible near-synonyms such as "circuitous", "direct" or "familiar" to make it a real test.

[minor] "Cautious → careful" with hasty/reckless/confident as distractors is far too trivial for BITSAT level; replace with a less transparent target word (e.g. "circumspect" or "prudent") or harder options.

[major] Option B (PRQS) also yields a fully grammatical sentence — "after its members had reviewed in detail the revised budget proposal before the final meeting" — since the adverbial may precede a long object, so the key is not uniquely defensible and the sentence must be recast (e.g. shorten the object or remove the movable adverbial).

Logical Reasoning: The section spans the expected BITSAT logical-reasoning topics (series, analogy, syllogism, coding, blood relations, cubes, word formation, classification) with no two items testing the same skill, and the keys for the verifiable items (99, 100, 103, 104, 105) are correct. Difficulty is skewed toward the very easy end (98 and 105 are near-instant), while 104 is the only demanding item and its ten-word count sits at the upper limit of the 90-second budget. The main production issue is the missing artwork for 102; the figure-based items 96 and 101 must be checked against their actual diagrams before printing.

[minor] Conclusion I is a word-for-word restatement of the first premise, so it tests nothing; replace it with a genuine inference (e.g. "Some artists are painters") while keeping the possibility conclusion.
[minor] The coding rule is stated outright and MAP needs only direct alphabet positions, making the item far too trivial for BITSAT; introduce a shift, reversal or reordering step.
[major] Options (A)–(D) are empty and no figure is supplied, so the odd-figure-out item is unanswerable as printed.

[minor] "Using each letter ... at most once" is ambiguous because INTERCHANGEABLE repeats A, E and N, and a literal reading rules out charitable/reachable/changeable (two A's) and gives 3, which is not an option; reword to "each letter may be used only as many times as it appears in the given word".

Mathematics: All 45 keys check out on independent reworking (including the trickier ones: 106 → D, 119 → 8400, 133 → 15−20i, 134 → 63A−62I, 141 → 3), and no item has a second defensible option or missing data. Topic spread is reasonable, though Integral Calculus is slightly over-weighted (five items) and the overall difficulty leans easy, with only 119, 127, 133, 138 and 141 demanding real multi-step work while 108, 139 and 142 are near-recall. Fix the two corrupted LaTeX strings and the q121 phrasing, and consider upgrading one or two of the trivial items to keep the paper's discrimination up.

[minor] Below BITSAT level: with identical z-coordinates the item collapses to spotting a 3-4-5 triple in one step, so it needs a twist (e.g. a point on an axis equidistant from two given points) to be worth a slot.
[minor] The LaTeX is corrupted — the opening math contains a NUL character instead of the backslash of \displaystyle ("$\0displaystyle\int"), which will print as garbage.
[minor] "An antiderivative of ∫x ln x dx is" is unidiomatic (an antiderivative of an integral) and contradicts the "+C" carried by every option; reword as "∫ x ln x dx equals".
[minor] Same corrupted math delimiter as q111: a NUL character precedes \dfrac{dy}{dx} in the stem and must be repaired before printing.
